Done for the room notes. For transportation, compact rental at MSN would be pickup Sunday after arrival, around 6:45 p.m., and return Thursday around 10:15 a.m. Current estimate is about $250 before fuel. Rideshares would not save much once you count airport and campus trips.
Compact is fine. Please don’t put me in a huge SUV unless they upgrade me for free and I have no choice.
Compact it is. I’ll also build the campus commute with a little buffer: Middleton to the lab is about 18-22 minutes in normal morning traffic, but we still need the visitor parking instructions.
Okay, book it.

Booked plan: Sunday July 27 DEN-MSN through Minneapolis, departing early afternoon and arriving Madison early evening; Thursday July 31 MSN-DEN through Minneapolis, departing around midday and arriving Denver late afternoon. Economy, not basic. Window seats selected where available, subject to aircraft changes.

Hotel reserved at the Middleton suite property Sunday-Thursday in a quiet king room, fridge noted, cancellable until July 24. Compact rental reserved at MSN for Sunday evening pickup and Thursday morning return.
Anything still hanging on the organizer?

Only campus logistics: visitor parking lot, permit process, and whether you need any lab-specific gear beyond laptop and closed-toe shoes. Everything else is set around the calmer Thursday return. Recheck seats at 24-hour check-in, and keep the hotel cancellation deadline in case the workshop changes.

Five days out for Madison and the airline just moved my Sunday Denver departure later. The Minneapolis connection is now about 40 minutes. There’s a no-cost switch to an earlier Denver flight. Should I take it?

I would. The current version gives you very little room at MSP, and Sunday weather around Minneapolis looks unsettled enough that a small delay could matter. The earlier Denver departure restores a connection around 90 minutes and gets you into Madison earlier. Unless leaving midday creates a work problem, it’s the better setup.
No work problem. Does switching mess up the rental car or hotel?

No major issue. The rental can keep the same reservation; just update the arriving flight number and note that pickup may be closer to 6 p.m. instead of later. The hotel already reconfirmed the quiet-room note, fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room, so an earlier arrival is fine.
Okay, take the earlier flight. Also my return seat map looks different and my window seat disappeared.

That’s from an aircraft swap on the return. After the earlier outbound switch, I see free window options on both Sunday segments. For Thursday, MSN-MSP has no free standard windows left, but there is a preferred window for $18; MSP-DEN still has a free window. Do you want the $18 window, or should I take a free aisle and keep watching?
Pay the $18 if that’s the only return window. I’d rather not risk a middle seat.

Done. Earlier outbound confirmed. Seats now show DEN-MSP 16A, MSP-MSN 8F, MSN-MSP 9A with the $18 preferred-seat charge, and MSP-DEN 18F. I’d still recheck at 24-hour check-in in case the airline shuffles anything again.
The workshop site sent parking instructions too. Visitor permit each day, lot behind the lab building. Can you sanity-check the timing?

For Monday, leave the Middleton hotel around 7:10 a.m. That gives you time for traffic, finding the visitor lot, and walking in before the 8:00 start. Buy or activate the daily permit the night before if the system allows it, then screenshot the permit/QR code. Tuesday and Wednesday you can probably leave closer to 7:20, but I’d keep Monday padded.
And Thursday return?

Leave the hotel around 9:35-9:45 a.m., top off gas if needed, return the compact at MSN around 10:15, and head inside for the 12:10-ish departure. With the Thursday return, you don’t need to touch the airport Wednesday after the final module.
Hotel reconfirmed quiet room and fridge. Any reason to call them again?

No need unless your Sunday arrival slips past about 10 p.m. You have the important pieces confirmed: quiet king room, fridge, free parking, and the pool/hot tub/fitness setup. Keep the confirmation email handy at check-in.
Give me the final pack and logistics list, then I’m done thinking about it.

Final Madison checklist: bring laptop, charger, workshop confirmation, photo ID, any analyzer training notes, closed-toe shoes, and a light layer for the lab room. Pack workout clothes and a swimsuit if you want to use the hotel amenities. Add a rain shell or compact umbrella for Sunday/Monday storms.

Before leaving: update the rental reservation with the new arriving flight number, save the campus parking permit instructions, screenshot hotel and car confirmations, and check in for flights at 24 hours. Monday morning, leave Middleton by 7:10 and expect the first parking attempt to take a few extra minutes.
Madison is off my plate. I need to look at Arizona next. The Phoenix metro training week is still squishy, and I’m considering tacking on Sedona with Mark if it doesn’t make the work week weird.

Sure. Let’s build a provisional plan and keep the risky pieces visible. What do you know so far: first required time and city, the clinic locations, the last in-person obligation, when Mark could arrive, and how long you’d want in Sedona?

Monday 2 p.m. setup at a reference lab in Tempe. Tuesday and Wednesday clinic sessions may split between Scottsdale and Mesa, order TBD. Thursday is either a Glendale wrap-up or a remote debrief. If we do Sedona, Friday to Monday is my thought. Mark could fly into Phoenix Thursday night or maybe Friday morning.

Given a Monday 2 p.m. setup, I’d be careful about flying in Monday unless you are very comfortable with a morning arrival and no disruption. Would you rather arrive Sunday and settle in? Also, should the work hotel be central to the Tempe/Mesa/Scottsdale triangle, or closer to whichever site ends up being first?
I’d rather go Sunday. Afternoon from Denver is better than a morning scramble, and nonstop should be easy to Phoenix. United or Southwest are fine; don’t pick a worse schedule just for the airline.

For your outbound, I’d rank it: 1) Sunday early-afternoon United nonstop DEN-PHX, arriving midafternoon; cleanest for check-in and a normal evening. 2) Southwest midafternoon nonstop; also fine, with the bag/change flexibility trade-off and no assigned seats. 3) A later low-fare nonstop; cheaper, but it turns Sunday into a late arrival. For the Sedona version, the return should be a Monday early-to-mid-afternoon PHX-DEN nonstop so you can drive down from Sedona with buffer.
For Mark, is Thursday night or Friday morning smarter?

Thursday night is the better experience if his workday allows it. Even if Glendale is in person and ends around 4, you could get back toward Tempe, regroup, and pick him up at PHX that evening. Friday morning may be cheaper, but it burns the start of your Sedona day and creates more waiting around Phoenix. I’d only choose Friday if Thursday becomes too late or too expensive.
That’s what I’m thinking. For the work hotel I want practical. No resort fee drama, and I don’t want to move midweek unless there’s a real reason.

Work-hotel shortlist: 1) Tempe suite property: strong guest score, free parking, fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness access; best central anchor for Tempe and Mesa, acceptable for Scottsdale and Glendale. 2) Scottsdale hotel: closer if Tuesday is Scottsdale, but resort fees and paid parking make it less clean. 3) Airport hotel: useful only for a late arrival or very early departure; worse for the clinic loop. I’d hold the Tempe suite through Friday checkout while the schedule firms up.
Tempe suite property sounds right. Rating over 4 is fine, and I’d use the pool or gym after training. Hot tub is a plus after being on my feet. Please note quiet king and fridge.

I’ll use that as the work-hotel target. For Sedona, I’d compare three types: 1) West Sedona resort-style hotel with a strong rating, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and cancellable king rooms where balcony can be requested. 2) Uptown/boutique option with better walkability and some balcony-view rooms, but weaker workout or hot-tub setup. 3) Village/Bell Rock option with a lower rate and good amenities, but less of the classic Sedona-room feel. My first choice is the cancellable West Sedona option if Mark is likely.
Yes, don’t lock us into a nonrefundable view room. What about the car? I’ll be driving between those sites, then probably up to Sedona.

I’d pick up at PHX Sunday and keep one vehicle through Monday. A compact or midsize sedan is enough for work-only, but it gets less appealing with two people, bags, and Sedona heat. Midsize SUV is the balanced choice. Standard SUV is more comfortable if Mark brings hiking gear or you want easier cargo space. If reimbursement stops Friday, it is still cleaner to split the cost than swap cars mid-trip.
Midsize SUV may be enough, but if Mark comes Thursday with hiking stuff I can see standard being easier. What schedule questions do I need answered before I push approvals?

Ask for: the exact Tempe setup address; the Tuesday/Wednesday site order; whether Thursday is definitely Glendale or remote; the Glendale address and target end time; whether any Friday debrief, gear return, or materials shipment is expected; and whether you need to carry anything bulky. Separately, get Mark’s latest workable Thursday flight and the Sedona cancellation deadline.
Give me the provisional recommendation in order. I need something I can paste into my notes.

Ranked plan: 1) Full extension plan: Erin flies Sunday afternoon nonstop DEN-PHX, stays at the Tempe suite hotel Sunday through Friday, keeps one midsize or standard SUV, Mark flies in Thursday evening, Sedona Friday to Monday, both return Monday early-to-mid-afternoon nonstop. Best overall if Thursday ends by about 4. 2) Hedge plan: book only cancellable hotels and your flight now, wait on Mark and Sedona until Thursday is confirmed. 3) Work-only plan: Tempe hotel, return Thursday evening or Friday morning, no Sedona. Use this only if Glendale or Friday obligations stay uncertain.
Use #1 as the working plan. Mark can answer tomorrow. I’m going to ask the coordinator now—can you word the questions so I don’t sound like I’m planning vacation on their time?

Send this: To finalize travel, can you confirm the Monday Tempe setup address and time, the Tuesday and Wednesday clinic locations and order, and whether Thursday will be an in-person Glendale wrap-up or remote debrief? If Glendale is in person, what end time should I plan around? Also, is there any Friday debrief, equipment return, or bulky material I should account for in the rental car? For Mark: If you can take a Thursday evening DEN-PHX nonstop, we can keep the Sedona weekend intact; Friday morning is cheaper but cuts into the day.
One more: I do not want to discover later that the good flight home is a red-eye or some annoying connection. Build around a sane Monday return if we do Sedona.

Agreed. For the Sedona version, I’d only use a Monday PHX-DEN nonstop leaving early-to-mid afternoon. That gives you breakfast in Sedona, a buffered drive to Phoenix, fuel and rental return time, and no late-night arrival. Next decision once Mark confirms: your Sunday afternoon outbound, his Thursday evening inbound, the shared Monday return, Tempe suite hold, cancellable Sedona hold, and SUV class.

Coordinator came back. Monday setup is Tempe at 2, Tuesday Scottsdale, Wednesday Mesa, Thursday Glendale in person but they expect to wrap by 4. No Friday debrief. Mark can do a Thursday evening flight or a cheaper Friday morning one. I’d like to book before the Sedona cancellable rate disappears.

Great, that makes the extension workable. I’d book your Sunday afternoon nonstop to Phoenix, Tempe suite hotel through Friday checkout, Mark’s Thursday evening nonstop, Sedona Friday to Monday, and one shared Monday nonstop home. The two remaining choices are Mark’s arrival and SUV size. Thursday costs more than Friday, but preserves the whole Sedona Friday.
Let’s compare Mark one more time. If Thursday lands too late, I don’t want a miserable pickup.

Thursday option: after-work nonstop, landing around 8 p.m. local, about $120 more than Friday. You would finish Glendale, head back toward Tempe, then pick him up without rushing dinner. Friday option: cheaper morning nonstop, but you either wait near Phoenix or get to Sedona closer to midday or early afternoon. I’d take Thursday unless his workday slips.
Book Thursday. For mine, use the Sunday afternoon nonstop that lands with enough time to check in and not the late budget flight.

Selected: your Sunday early-afternoon DEN-PHX nonstop, arriving midafternoon, and Mark’s Thursday evening DEN-PHX nonstop. For the shared return, I’m holding a Monday early-afternoon PHX-DEN nonstop. I’ll request a window for your solo outbound; for the shared return, do you want adjacent seats prioritized over window seats?
Yes. On the return, together matters more than both windows.

Car choice: midsize SUV is the cheaper balanced option; standard SUV is more comfortable for two bags, hiking gear, and summer driving, and both hotels have parking covered. I’d choose standard SUV if Mark is bringing trail gear, with midsize SUV as the fallback if inventory gets tight.
Standard SUV, with midsize SUV as fallback. No sedan unless there’s no choice and you ask me.

Hotels are ready to confirm: Tempe suite property Sunday through Friday checkout, quiet king away from elevator, fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Sedona Friday through Monday, cancellable king room, balcony/high-floor request, pool, hot tub, and fitness access. The cancellable Sedona rate expires tonight. Lock it?
Yes, lock the cancellable Sedona room. Don’t pay for a guaranteed view if it makes the rate nonrefundable.

I’ll book the cancellable room and add balcony/high-floor as a request only. For payment split: work card for your airfare, Tempe hotel, and the work portion of the rental; personal card for Mark’s flight, Sedona, and the weekend portion. If the rental has to stay on one card, I’ll note the work-versus-personal split in the itinerary.
That split works. Use the same cards as last time.

Booked. Summary: you have a Sunday afternoon DEN-PHX nonstop; Mark has a Thursday evening DEN-PHX nonstop; you both return Monday early afternoon PHX-DEN nonstop. Tempe suite hotel is confirmed through Friday checkout with quiet king, fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Sedona is confirmed Friday to Monday on the cancellable king rate with balcony/high-floor request. Standard SUV is booked from PHX Sunday to Monday, with midsize SUV fallback noted. Seats requested: window on your solo outbound, adjacent seats together on the shared return.
What remains before I can stop poking at this?

Only operational items: get the exact Glendale address, recheck seat maps at check-in, confirm Mark’s bag count, and save the Sedona cancellation deadline. Calendar timing: land Sunday midafternoon; Monday setup at 2 p.m.; Tuesday Scottsdale; Wednesday Mesa; Thursday Glendale ends around 4, then airport pickup; Friday checkout and drive to Sedona after rush hour; Monday leave Sedona by about 9:30 for PHX, fuel, SUV return, and the early-afternoon flight home.

Five days out and Arizona is doing the last-minute thing. Mark’s inbound moved 50 minutes later, the return aircraft swap split our seats, Tempe says the hot tub is closed, Sedona says balcony is still request-only but they’ll sell me a guaranteed first-floor patio, and the rental app is warning limited SUVs. What actually needs changing?

Not much needs changing. Keep Mark’s flight, but treat Thursday as airport pickup plus snacks, not dinner. Keep Tempe unless the commute matters less than the hot tub, which I don’t think it does. Decide whether the patio upcharge is worth it, fix the return seats, and protect the SUV reservation.
Keep Tempe. Annoying about the hot tub, but I’m not moving to a worse commute and paid parking. What do you think on the Sedona patio?

I’d skip the paid patio if it is only first-floor access and not a view guarantee. With heat and possible smoke, balcony time may be limited anyway. Keep the king room with high-floor/balcony request and ask again at check-in.
Agreed. On seats, take the one window and the adjacent aisle if that keeps us together. Keep my outbound window if it’s untouched.
Your outbound window is still set. For the Monday return, only one nearby window remains; do you want that assigned to you or Mark?
Give Mark the return window. I’ll take the aisle next to him.

Done. Rental plan: keep the standard SUV reservation, check in online before you fly, and go to the desk if the app offers a downgrade. Accept a midsize SUV or crossover only with a rate adjustment confirmed; decline a sedan unless you approve it.
Last thing: heat and smoke. I don’t want a rigid hiking plan.

Use an early-and-flexible plan: Friday drive up and do only an easy overlook; Saturday start at sunrise and be off exposed trails by 10, with Tlaquepaque, Chapel area, pool time, or a spa slot as backups; Sunday choose a shorter creek or scenic-drive option if haze is bad. Pack N95s, electrolytes, sun sleeves, and extra water for the SUV. Monday leave Sedona by 9:00-9:30, fuel near Phoenix, return the SUV, and recheck seats at check-in.

Arizona is finally off my desk. I got invited to a veterinary diagnostics education summit in Indianapolis in mid-September, and I need help sketching flights and hotel before I say yes to the travel budget.
Sure. Send me the agenda anchors and what you know about the hotel setup. I’ll keep it to a short ranked plan rather than a giant fare dump.

Badge pickup and a reception are Monday evening. Supplier lab sessions start Tuesday morning. The final hands-on demo is Thursday and may run late enough that I’m worried about a Thursday flight home. I’d be flying Denver to Indianapolis.

That gives us three practical decisions: the Monday outbound, whether to come home Thursday night or Friday, and whether the conference hotel is worth taking over a better-amenity property. For DEN-IND, I’m seeing a Monday afternoon nonstop that arrives before the reception, plus a cheaper one-stop with a longer sit. The return can be done Thursday evening, but it looks dependent on how late that demo actually runs.
Give me the ranked version. I also want to know if the hot tub/pool/fitness trade-off is worth rideshares. I’m fine walking if the attached hotel is solid.

Flight ranking first: 1. Monday afternoon nonstop outbound plus Friday late-morning return. Best balance: simple outbound, no racing from the Thursday demo, and still only one extra hotel night. 2. Monday afternoon nonstop plus Thursday evening return. Cheaper on hotel nights, but only comfortable if the demo ends on time and you can go straight to the airport. 3. Cheaper one-stop outbound plus Friday return. It saves some money, but the connection is long enough that it eats the value unless the fare gap gets much bigger. I would not build this around a long connection just to save a modest amount.
No rental car unless there’s a real reason. What does Monday look like with the nonstop?

The nonstop is the clean one: leave Denver in the early-to-mid afternoon, land in Indianapolis a little before 6 local time, then take a rideshare straight to the convention-center area. If badge pickup runs into the evening, that should work with some buffer. The one-stop option lands later after a long connection, so it only makes sense if the reception timing is flexible or the fare difference becomes meaningful.
Badge pickup says 6 to 8 and the reception is roughly 6:30 to 8:30. I can miss the first few minutes. I don’t want a two-hour airport sit just to save $90.

Then I’d treat the Monday nonstop as the working outbound. Hotel ranking: 1. Convention-center block: strongest for the actual summit, guest score around the low 4s, attached or very easy walk, fitness room, indoor pool, no hot tub. 2. Suite property a short rideshare away: lower nightly rate, pool, hot tub, and fitness access, likely more comfortable for decompression, but you’ll add rideshares and lose the easy networking/drop-in convenience. 3. Airport hotel: only useful if you were arriving very late or staging for a flight; it does not help the summit days.
For a conference, attached usually wins. But if the block is mediocre I’d rather sleep at the suite property. Is the block above that basic business-hotel bar?

It looks acceptable rather than fancy. The useful points are the guest score, walkability, and not having to commute before the Tuesday labs. I’d want to confirm the room type, cancellation window, and whether they can note a quiet room. The amenity gap is real: indoor pool and fitness room are covered, hot tub is not. If hot tub recovery is the deciding factor, the suite property wins; if the summit schedule is the deciding factor, the block wins.
Can you put this into a decision version? What needs confirming before booking?

Yes. Before booking, confirm five things. First, badge pickup really stays open until at least 7:30 or 8, because that supports the Monday nonstop. Second, get the Thursday demo hard stop or expected end time; if it may run past 4:30, Friday return is the calmer choice. Third, check the hotel block cutoff, cancellation terms, quiet king availability, and fridge request. Fourth, ask whether any demo materials need shipping or if carrying them from the hotel is fine. Fifth, confirm there is no offsite lab location that would require a car. If all sessions are in or near the convention center, rideshares are enough.
What about Thursday return if I really want to be home Thursday? Is it impossible or just unpleasant?

Not impossible, but it’s a narrow lane. If the last workable flight leaves around early evening and the demo runs to 4:45, you’d need bags already handled, a quick exit from the session, a rideshare with no wait, and no security surprise. You’d also skip any debrief or late networking. If the demo ends closer to 4, it becomes more reasonable. If the demo timing is uncertain, Thursday night is the stress option.
I’d rather not bolt from the lab, but I also don’t love paying another night.

The extra night may partly wash out if the Friday return prices better than the Thursday evening flight. Even if it costs more overall, it buys you a clean demo finish, dinner without watching the clock, and a normal airport morning. For a summit where Thursday is the final hands-on piece, I’d lean Friday unless the coordinator confirms an earlier end.
Any reason United matters on this route?

On this route, United is relevant because it has one of the cleaner Denver nonstop options. I would use it if the timing and price stay close. I would not choose a United connection over a better nonstop or a much cleaner return; schedule simplicity is the driver here.
Okay. Tentative plan: Monday afternoon nonstop, probably Friday return, convention block unless the hot tub place is massively better. Can you give me the exact questions to send the coordinator?

Send this: Can you confirm Monday badge pickup hours and whether arriving around 6:15-6:30 is still fine? What is the realistic Thursday demo end time, and is attendance expected through the end? Are all Tuesday-Thursday sessions at the convention center or attached hotel area? For the hotel block, is there a quiet king available, what is the cancellation deadline, and can a fridge be requested? Are the indoor pool and fitness room open during the summit dates, and is it correct that there is no hot tub? Finally, should demo cases be carried in by attendees or shipped to the show desk? Once those answers come back, I’d be ready to book the Monday nonstop, decide Thursday versus Friday, and skip the car unless they name an offsite location.

The Indianapolis coordinator answered. Badge pickup is open until 7:30 Monday, Tuesday starts at 8:30, and the Thursday demo could run until 4:45. The hotel block cutoff is coming up. Can we decide now?

Yes. With those times, the Monday afternoon nonstop is the clear outbound. It now prices close to the one-stop, so there’s no good reason to add the longer connection. For the return, Friday late morning is the cleaner pick; Thursday evening would require leaving almost straight from the demo. Hotel-wise, the block is still the convenience winner: guest score around 4.2, quiet king available to request, indoor pool and fitness room, but no hot tub.
Give me the booking version. I want the least annoying week, not an optimization over $50.

Book the Monday Denver to Indianapolis nonstop that lands before badge pickup closes. Pair it with a Friday late-morning Indianapolis to Denver return so Thursday can run long without turning into a sprint. Reserve the convention-center block before the cutoff, with quiet king, away from elevators or ice if possible, and fridge request. Skip the rental car unless your demo kit turns into more than you can reasonably roll into the hotel.
Yes, choose the nonstop on the outbound. Is Friday worth the extra hotel night?

Given the 4:45 possible demo end, yes. A Thursday flight means packed bags, no lingering questions, no post-demo conversation, and a direct dash to the airport. Friday gives you a normal close to the summit and a calmer morning ride to IND. If the fare difference is close, the extra hotel night is buying schedule control rather than luxury.
Okay, Friday. Hotel is my last hesitation. I keep thinking about the no hot tub piece, but walking to everything may matter more.

For this summit, I’d take the block. The suite property is the better wellness-amenity match because it has pool, hot tub, and fitness access, plus the lower rate. But the block keeps you steps from the 8:30 start, badge pickup, reception, and any hallway networking. Since the block still has the pool and fitness room and a decent guest score, the missing hot tub is the trade-off I’d accept here.
Book the block if it’s cancelable until at least a couple days before arrival. Add quiet room away from elevators and a fridge if that’s allowed.

I’ll reserve the block under those terms if available: quiet king, away from elevators/ice, fridge requested, Monday evening arrival noted. I’ll also keep the suite property as the backup until the block confirmation and cancellation language are clear.
Do I need a rental car? I’ll have one demo kit but not a full booth.

No rental car for this version. Airport rideshare to the hotel, then walking for the summit days. Parking would be wasted money, and downtown driving adds more friction than value. If the demo kit gets heavy or awkward, shipping it to the show desk is better than renting a car just to move one case.
Please also make sure I’m not stuck in a middle seat.
Window or aisle for these legs if both are available?
Window if it’s open. Aisle only if the only window is in the last row.

Got it. I’ll book the Monday nonstop outbound, the Friday late-morning return, select or request window seats that are not last-row seats, reserve the convention-center block with the quiet king and fridge notes, and leave the car off the plan. Open follow-ups after booking: save the hotel cancellation deadline, watch for schedule changes, and ask the coordinator for demo-kit shipping instructions if the case gets any bulkier.
Six days out for Indianapolis. I got a schedule-change email, and the seat map looks weird. Can you sanity-check the last logistics?

Yes. The outbound moved 28 minutes later, but it still works for badge pickup if you go straight from IND to the hotel by rideshare. Do not wait around for a shuttle. The aircraft swap is why the window seat disappeared; I’ll recheck for another acceptable window and avoid moving you into a middle seat.
I also have one demo case. The convention email says the loading zone is going to be a mess Monday.

Then ship that case to the show desk if they’ll accept it. Ask for the label format, receiving hours, and pickup location. It will be much easier than managing a case through airport rideshare pickup and a crowded hotel arrival.
Hotel confirmed the quiet king note and the fridge request. Same story: pool and fitness room, no hot tub.
Good. That keeps the hotel plan intact. Monday arrival should be rideshare, check in, drop your bag, then badge pickup before 7:30. If the flight slips at all, badge pickup comes before dinner.
What time should I leave for DEN?

Aim to be at DEN about two hours before the new departure. If the flight is now just after 2, leave home around 11:15 to 11:30. Since the demo case should ship separately, you can keep the airport day to your carry-on and laptop bag.
And dinner? I won’t have bandwidth for anything complicated after that later arrival.

Keep it simple: hotel bar or a nearby casual place after badge pickup, with an airport snack as the backup if the arrival slips. I’ll recheck seats at the 24-hour mark, confirm the demo-case shipping instructions, and set the Friday plan as rideshare to IND around 8:45-9:00 for the late-morning flight home.

Indianapolis is finally off my desk. I need to start looking at the Sacramento clinic loop for October, but the order is still mushy. Can you help me think through flight, hotel base, and car before I commit to anything?
Yes. Give me the rough week and what you know about the sites so far. I can frame it as a few trip shapes rather than pretending the schedule is locked.

Week of October 20. Denver to Sacramento. Monday afternoon setup at a Sacramento reference lab is tentative, Tuesday likely Davis, Wednesday maybe Roseville, and Thursday could be a Stockton install or just a remote recap. I do not want to book until I know the Thursday piece.

There are three sensible flight shapes. First: fly Denver to Sacramento on the Sunday afternoon nonstop, arrive early evening, get the car, and have a calm Monday morning before the lab setup. Second: take a Monday morning nonstop, which saves one hotel night but gives you very little cushion if the flight slips or the lab wants you earlier. Third: use a one-stop itinerary to save money, but that adds risk without helping the training week much. For the return, Thursday evening can work only if Stockton ends on time; Friday late morning or midday is cleaner and costs one extra hotel night.
Price both Thursday and Friday for now. I’d rather not do an ugly connection unless the savings are real. What about where to stay?

For bases, I’d shortlist three. The Roseville suite property is the strongest all-around stay: good guest feedback, free parking, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and rooms with a fridge. It is very convenient for Wednesday and decent for Sacramento, but less convenient for Davis and Stockton. The Capitol-area Sacramento hotel is better geographically for Monday and a little easier for Davis/Stockton, but parking is paid and it does not have a hot tub. The airport hotel only makes sense if you arrive late and want to crash near SMF; I would not use it as the base for the whole loop.
How bad are the drives from Roseville? I can tolerate imperfect if the hotel is better, but I do not want a 90-minute morning every day.

Approximate drive pattern: SMF to Roseville is about 25 to 30 minutes. Roseville to the Sacramento lab is usually 25 to 40 depending on the exact lab address. Roseville to Davis is more like 45 to 60 in the morning. Roseville to Stockton is the stretch, roughly 75 to 90-plus if traffic is unkind. From a Capitol-area hotel, Davis and Stockton are each meaningfully easier, but you trade into paid parking and weaker amenities.
Monday is probably a 1:30 setup, so Roseville after a Sunday arrival might be okay. Davis at 8 on Tuesday is the one that makes me twitchy.

If Davis really starts at 8:00, Roseville means leaving around 6:50 or 7:00 to avoid sweating it. From downtown Sacramento you might leave closer to 7:15. So the question is whether saving 20 to 25 minutes Tuesday morning is worth losing the easier parking and better recovery setup. For one Davis morning, Roseville is still reasonable; I would confirm the Tuesday start time before booking it.
Remind me what the Capitol hotel loses besides parking.

It is closer to the Monday lab and restaurants, but the trade-offs are real: paid parking, no hot tub, smaller room footprint, and the fridge is request-only rather than a reliable suite feature. Guest feedback is fine, not bad, just not as strong as the Roseville suite option.
Roseville sounds less annoying overall. What about the rental? I may have one analyzer case, and if Stockton is live it could be two.

If it is one analyzer case plus your normal bag, a compact could work. If there is any chance of two cases, I’d move to midsize. The price difference is usually modest, and the trunk space matters when you are moving cases between clinic sites. Pickup at SMF on Sunday is straightforward; drop-off timing depends on Thursday versus Friday return.
What do the actual flight times look like?

Representative options: Sunday afternoon nonstop Denver to Sacramento, roughly 2:00 to 3:45 p.m. local arrival, is the cleanest outbound. Monday morning nonstop is roughly 8:30 to 10:10 a.m.; workable only if the lab setup stays at 1:30 and nothing slips. Coming home, a Thursday evening nonstop around 6:30 p.m. is possible after Stockton if you are done by 3:00, but it leaves little room for a late install, gas, car return, and security. Friday late morning or midday is much calmer. The cheaper one-stop returns I’m seeing are not attractive for this week because they push you late and add connection exposure.
I do not want a near-midnight one-stop after Stockton. Keep it on the sheet as a no unless finance starts yelling.

Then my preliminary ranking is: first, Sunday afternoon nonstop outbound, Roseville base, midsize rental, and Friday return if Thursday is truly Stockton. Second, same outbound and hotel but Thursday evening return only if Thursday becomes remote or a very short wrap-up. Third, Monday morning outbound only if the coordinator confirms there is no morning prep, no case pickup, and a forgiving lab arrival window.
Before I commit, give me the confirmation questions for the coordinator. Include whether I actually need to be in Stockton Thursday.

Send this: Can you confirm the final site order for the week of October 20: Monday Sacramento lab setup, Tuesday Davis, Wednesday Roseville, and Thursday Stockton? What are the exact start and expected end times for each site, especially Davis Tuesday morning and Stockton Thursday? For Monday, is 1:30 p.m. firm, and is any morning prep, badge access, or equipment pickup required? For Thursday, do I need to be physically present in Stockton, or can the wrap-up be handled remotely if the install is stable? If Stockton is in person, what is the realistic latest end time? Finally, will I be carrying one analyzer case or two, and are there any site parking or loading dock instructions I should know before booking the rental and hotel base?

The California coordinator answered. Monday is a 1:30 Sacramento lab setup, Tuesday Davis, Wednesday Roseville, and Thursday Stockton with a 3:00-ish finish if the install behaves. The Roseville suite hotel can hold a quiet king with fridge until tomorrow. The Capitol hotel lost the cancellable rate in policy. I need to settle this.

With that sequence, I would lock the Sunday afternoon nonstop into Sacramento, use the Roseville suite hotel, and reserve a midsize car. The return is the only real decision. Thursday evening nonstop is doable if Stockton ends at 3:00, but it is tight after the drive, fuel, car return, and security. Friday midday is calmer and adds one hotel night.
Friday morning is open. I have a 3:30 Denver-time call, but I can take it from home if the flight behaves. Is Friday return too padded?

I do not think it is over-padded for this version of the week. Thursday puts all the risk on the Stockton install ending cleanly. Friday lets you finish, drive back without racing, sleep near your base, and get to SMF without doing airport math from Stockton.
Okay, Friday return. Book Sunday outbound, Friday return, Roseville base, and a midsize car. What pickup and drop-off timing should I use?

Use SMF pickup around 4:15 p.m. Sunday, assuming the afternoon nonstop lands around 3:45. For Friday, return the car around 9:45 for a late-morning or midday flight. I’d keep the rental cancellable and choose midsize sedan or small SUV, not prepaid if the rate gap is small.
For seats, same as Indy: window if it is not the last row, aisle over a last-row window, and no middle.
Got it. I’ll request window seats away from the last row where available. If the only window is last row, I’ll take an aisle farther forward and recheck the map at check-in.
Any issue with sleeping in Roseville before Davis?

It is fine if you protect the morning. For an 8:00 Davis start, plan to leave Roseville around 6:50. Monday Sacramento should be about 30 to 40 minutes from Roseville, Wednesday is easy, and Thursday Stockton is the long one, so build extra buffer that morning.
Hotel notes?
